spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Nonvanishing is obtained by comparing conserved first-moment mass with an L2 capacity bound. On characters where L(s0,chi)=0, the basic equation removes the LM term and forces S to be explained by the controlled errors I+J; the remaining mass must therefore be carried by nonvanishing characters, whose number is bounded below by Cauchy-Schwarz.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The proof partitions nontrivial characters according to L(s0,chi)=0 or not in the identity S=LM+I+J. Proposition 4.1 supplies a large first moment for S; on the zero set S=I+J, whose total is bounded using the J estimate and Proposition 10.1 for I. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the contribution of the complementary set by its cardinality times the S second moment, and the sigma=1/2 case yields a positive lower proportion.
directed.conceptual_reading: The mollified identity acts as a detector with two complementary guarantees: total signal remains large, while zeros can account for only limited signal through controlled remainder terms. Nonvanishing becomes a population-counting consequence rather than a pointwise evaluation of individual L-values.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is first moment -> partition by the semantic event L=0 -> second-moment control -> cardinality. The intermediate object is the detector S, whose decomposition makes the zero condition algebraically useful.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument gives a positive proportion, not all characters, and the threshold in q may depend on the fixed point. This unit completes the critical-line subcase; exact lower-bound constants and OCR-damaged errors should not be asserted from it.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the moment-comparison and Cauchy-Schwarz logic; moderate confidence in parameter restrictions, and low confidence in the numerical proportion.

The coefficient-square sum is evaluated as a function f(j-2), with a separate treatment of the first relevant interval, and this gives a mean-square bound for the tail S*(sigma_j,chi)=S(sigma_j,chi)-1.

directed.boundary_or_failure: Decay depends on the chosen cutoff, circle geometry, and coefficient weights; it is not a generic consequence of any nearby zero. The contour display, exponents, and exact form of f are OCR-sensitive, and j=2 requires its own bound.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the Cauchy-transport and cutoff-tail mechanism; low confidence in exact decay formulas and constants.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proof modularizes local failure into three separately controlled quantities: the long detector tail S*, the variation of I from the zero to the interval center, and J. Their mean squares have different origins and decay profiles, but all fit the same final quadratic inequality.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit records the bound for S*=S-1 obtained from localization, derives an analogous Cauchy-circle estimate for the difference involving I using Proposition 10.1, splits that I estimate according to the size of j, and adds a separate negligible mean-square estimate for J. These are identified as the inputs needed when the basic equation is evaluated at sigma_j.
directed.conceptual_reading: Separating the three errors prevents one coarse estimate from obscuring which mechanism controls which term: coefficient tails control S*, the I-moment controls analytic variation, and an independent estimate disposes of J. The final argument can then combine commensurable L2 quantities.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Cauchy differences translate character-dependent zero locations to the common centers sigma_j. At those centers, S*, I, and J become a vector of error coordinates whose squared norms can be added and compared with the detector discrepancy |LM-1|.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The bounds are family averages and allow exceptional characters. The threshold separating j-regimes, the exponential rates, and constants in the displayed estimates are not reliable in the OCR text.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the three-term decomposition and their roles; low confidence in exact thresholds and quantitative constants.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The closure is a summability argument. At each circle, the basic equation turns a zero into a detector discrepancy bounded by the three localized errors; their exponential decay yields a summable bad-character proportion, and starting sufficiently far from the critical line makes the total strictly less than the whole family.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Returning to S=LM+I+J, the proof obtains a quadratic bound for |L(sigma_j,chi)M(sigma_j,chi)-1| in terms of |S*|^2, |I|^2, and |J|^2. The preceding estimates convert this into an upper bound for Z(j,q), the number of characters with a real zero in C_j. Summing over j>=j_0 and choosing an absolute j_0 sufficiently large makes the normalized total less than one, leaving a positive proportion with no real zero on the covered segment.
directed.conceptual_reading: Local control becomes uniform control because the failure probabilities are summable, not because a pointwise estimate is uniform. The proof spends a fixed amount of critical-strip width, encoded by j_0/log q, to make the union of all local bad events smaller than the population.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The final bridge is localized L2 error -> circle-wise bad-character count -> union bound over the cover -> positive-size zero-free subfamily. Exponential interval-index decay is the compression that makes infinitely many-looking local obligations manageable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion concerns a positive proportion of characters and real zeros in the specified segment for sufficiently large prime q. It does not prove a universal zero-free region, exclude nonreal zeros, or imply the Riemann hypothesis; exact numerical constants in the bad-character bound require scan verification.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the summability and positive-proportion conclusion; low confidence in the OCR-damaged numerical constants.
